response.prediction: Surgeons prevent major blood loss during coronary artery bypass surgery by using a heart-lung machine to temporarily stop the heart and cool it, which slows bleeding. They carefully control blood flow by clamping blood vessels and using precise surgical techniques to avoid damaging tissues. Medications like heparin are used to prevent clotting during the procedure but are closely managed to avoid excessive bleeding afterward. Surgeons also conserve blood by reusing the patient’s own blood when possible and ensure thorough hemostasis by applying pressure, suturing, and using clips to stop any bleeding at the surgical site. These steps work together to minimize blood loss and improve safety.
